name: air_separator
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Generate ONE final inventory sprite of a compact industrial air separation machine for a pixel-art game. Image 1 is the original game's style reference; Image 2 is a comparison sheet showing the rejected overly busy first design on the left and an overly flat hand-simplified concept in the middle/right. Use the concept's simple twin-column silhouette, with the original game's restrained dimensional metal shading. Do NOT reproduce the comparison sheet or any text. Deliver exactly one machine.
CRITICAL: Design at a true logical 48x48 pixel grid, then enlarge using nearest-neighbor. This is a tiny game icon, not an intricate miniature. About 12-14 flat colors, contiguous planes, 1-pixel outline in dusty dark violet; 2 or 3 flat tones per material. No dithering, gradients, isolated decorative noise, screws, repeated ribs, loops of thin pipes, tiny vents or fan spokes.
Machine: two broad upright rounded grey-green separation columns, a single wide blue band on the left and a muted sage-green band on the right. A short thick horizontal bridge connects their upper sections. Both columns merge into a SINGLE broad squat compressor housing at the bottom, with ONE large dark circular intake containing just three broad horizontal slats, and solid quiet side panels. In the middle between the columns is a small solid raised control housing above the intake with ONE small rectangular power indicator. No exposed external piping. Slight bevels and short restrained cream top-edge highlights provide volume; avoid a primitive flat diagram. Front view with a small visible top plane. Nearly square footprint, all nine centers of the 3x3 inventory grid must fall on opaque machine body (including the upper bridge and central control housing). Large, readable silhouette filling about 44 of the logical 48 pixels. Genuine transparent exterior. No text, no numbers, no scene, no floor, no cast shadow. Keep the central control indicator dark: powered variant will be a tiny deterministic pixel edit.
